title: Dose-Response Bounds for Circular Treatment Times Observed through Half-Circle Window Releases
banked_reason: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope. D0.5 math panel returned revise with three unrepaired findings.
gap_reasons: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope.

The mixed-harmonic target is used as a fixed policy weight without imposing its required Lipschitz membership: its actual Lipschitz constant must be bounded by the declared L_w (or this submodel must define a separate unrestricted policy class).

General endpoints are variational extrema with attainment but no implementable optimization procedure, and the package supplies no sampling inference, limiting its operational and reproducibility case.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived an exact release fiber, attained endpoint and worst-pair extrema, a class-level Q^-2 modulus with positive centered witnesses, and a certified unrestricted two-window cost switch in a small positive-L_f regime. D0.5 rated the delivered package subfield, below the required field floor, and found no bounded same-topic route to field. The math panel returned revise: the policy-weight Lipschitz admissibility condition and two deliverability/positioning findings remain open, so this bank is an archived research attempt, not a verified theorem; no Lean formalization was reached.
tldr: Under pointwise weak unconfoundedness, the additional diagonal mean condition \(\mathbb E[Y\mid\sigma(A)]=m(A)\), and a public uniform release origin independent of \(\sigma(A,Y,\{Y(a)\})\), a circular treatment time is observed only through a half-circle membership release. The added-release action set is intentionally rational; irrational population injectivity is prior art and lies outside this finite menu. Rational added windows never recover the full treatment density or response curve, but their common null frequencies have a much smaller effect on the weighted causal policy value \(\theta_w=\int wq/f\). The central theorem gives a uniform \(C_wQ^{-2}\) posterior-diameter bound and positive observationally equivalent causal models with matching \(Q^{-2}\) order. A compact indistinguishable-pair reduction makes release choice operational. The mixed-harmonic calculation gives exact values only in the known-uniform-density submodel; for the actual unrestricted risk at \(P_{\star}\), an explicit sandwich proves a genuine \(1/4\)-to-\(1/3\) cost switch whenever \(L_f<1/[2(\pi^2+1)]\) and brackets the exact tie price. Exact unrestricted diameter values, exact nonconstant-density menu values, and the leading high-resolution constant remain open, including inside the certified switch regime.
gap: Periodic boxcar theory characterizes lost frequencies and whole-signal recovery risk, while interval-data and optimal-recovery theory treats linear response functionals on fixed or convex classes. Marmarelis et al. (2023) instead bound continuous-treatment dose responses by relaxing ignorability through a hidden-confounding sensitivity model. None of these results quantifies the randomized release-coarsening fiber of the nonlinear causal ratio \(q/f\) under maintained weak unconfoundedness or uses its posterior modulus to choose a costed rational release.
fill: The project derives the exact complete-law fiber, compact causal endpoints, an ex ante pair-modulus representation, a matched \(Q^{-2}\) ratio-modulus theorem, and an exact target-harmonic window comparison with a cost threshold.
